answers.U1-S1: The flamingo's wings were a glorious crimson color when it opened them, making it look like the most angel-like creature on earth.
answers.U1-S2: He was young and scared of the cattle, so he only agreed to go once his brother promised to stay away from anything with horns.
answers.U1-S3: To show the plain was full of giant thistles and tall flowery grass, like an English meadow in June.
answers.U1-S4: Seriously and slowly, in a calm, dignified way.
answers.U1-S5: Because the open wings were a glorious crimson color, which was amazing to see against the white-and-rose body.
answers.U1-S6: The birds were rare in that area; nobody nearby knew them because the flamingos lived at a lake almost a day away.
answers.U1-S7: Because when it raised its long neck and spread its crimson wings, it looked heavenly and beautiful, like an angel.
answers.U1-S8: Later he saw them at sunset with reflections and flying in long crimson half-moon lines, but those weren't as amazing as the first.
answers.U1-S9: It describes the beautiful ways he later saw flamingos, like reflected in still water or flying in a crimson line over blue water.
answers.U1-S10: He remembers it fondly and with wonder, still amazed by the crimson-winged bird.
